title: The Crown of the Sundered Sea Anew
premise: Yara Halloran, a nonbinary bone-carver who hears the dead through their carvings, lives in the Valley of Stillness where magic cannot enter—until a prophecy book written a century ago names them as the bearer of the Sundered Crown on tonight's date. Dragged from hiding by a dying messenger and pursued by the Tidebound Court, Yara learns they are heir to both sides of an ancient war: the drowned queen's blood runs in them, and the crown can either raise the sunken kingdom or drown the coastlands forever. Hunted by their own half-sister, Admiral Serevan, who wants the crown to wage war on the land-dwellers, Yara gathers a found family of outcasts—a disgraced tide-priest, a smuggler captain, and a ghost who refuses to move on. In the climax beneath the sundered sea, Yara refuses both thrones and shatters the crown into the bones of the dead, giving every voice it held its own name again. The long winter breaks not through victory but through shared grief, and Yara returns home changed, no longer invisible but finally belonging.
about_author: Edmund Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck ledgers along a fog-bound coast before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about inheritance, grief, and the families we build when blood fails us.

chapters.title: The Book That Knew Tonight
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the magic-dead valley, Yara finishes carving a memorial bone for a client while hearing the dead murmur through their work. A peddler sells them a waterlogged prophecy book; inside, tonight's date names 'the Halloran bone-carver' as crown-bearer. Yara dismisses it as coincidence until the valley's stillness trembles for the first time in living memory. Beat: dread disguised as ordinary life cracking open.

chapters.title: A Messenger Drowns on Dry Land
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A half-drowned messenger crawls into Yara's workshop speaking of the Tidebound Court and pressing a shard of white coral into their hand before dying—yet his voice lingers, begging Yara to carry the secret north. Magic has breached the valley, meaning someone powerful wants Yara found. Beat: guilt and reluctant responsibility as Yara buries the man and packs a bag.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Lost His God
chapters.summary: Alternating Yara and Brother Fenwick's POV. Fleeing north, Yara is ambushed by tide-wraiths and saved by Fenwick, a defrocked tide-priest exiled for heresy: he claims the drowned queen was murdered by her own court. He recognizes the coral shard as a key. Beat: wary alliance between two people who've each been cast out for what they know.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Fenwick's POV. Sheltering in a cliffside ossuary, Fenwick watches Yara carve a whale vertebra and accidentally give voice to the bones' memories—the first time anyone has heard the drowned kingdom's history firsthand. The dead reveal the crown was never a symbol of rule but a prison holding ten thousand souls. Beat: wonder curdling into horror at what Yara carries.

chapters.title: Captain Vess of the Salt-Luck
chapters.summary: Vess's POV introduced mid-chase. Smuggler captain Odessa Vess agrees to ferry them across the Sundered Strait—for a price: Yara must raise the voice of her brother, lost with a sunk fleet, so she can hear his last words. What he says instead implicates Vess's own family in the old betrayal. Beat: found family forming around shared wounds and bad bargains.

chapters.title: My Sister's Navy
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The Salt-Luck is boarded by the royal navy of the coastlands—and its admiral is Serevan, Yara's estranged half-sister, who has read the same prophecy and believes seizing the crown will save the land from the long winter. She offers Yara a place beside her. Beat: heartbreak as Yara realizes their only blood family stands on the wrong side of mercy.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Escaping Serevan, the crew sails into a supernatural winter that freezes the sea solid, trapping the ship. As supplies fail, the ghost of the drowned queen begins speaking through Yara's carvings—not commanding, but pleading. Fenwick's faith cracks; Vess considers mutiny. Beat: despair and the test of whether this fragile family holds under pressure.

chapters.title: Beneath the Sundered Sea
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Guided by the queen's ghost, Yara dives through a breathing-hole into the sunken capital, where the crown rests on an altar of ribs. Serevan follows, and the sisters confront each other among the dead. When Serevan seizes the crown, the imprisoned souls begin tearing free, threatening to drag both kingdoms under. Beat: terror at the brink of the ancient war reigniting.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax. Rather than claim or destroy the crown outright, Yara does what they have always done: carves. Using their gift, they speak each soul's true name back to it, unbinding the crown from within as Serevan, confronted by the murdered queen's memory, finally lets go. The war ends not in triumph but in a vast, released chorus. Beat: sacrifice transmuted into witness; power refused.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers Me
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, resolution. Winter breaks. Serevan, stripped of rank, chooses exile and asks—awkwardly—to write letters. Fenwick rebuilds his faith around the named dead; Vess sails home lighter. Yara returns to the valley, which now hums faintly with magic, and opens a workshop where the living can commission carvings to hear their own dead say goodbye. Beat: quiet belonging; inheritance remade as gift rather than burden.
